point_observation_warning.statement: Neither dataset publishes an instantaneous point observation. Every published record of every selected variable is an interval statistic over its native reporting interval.
point_observation_warning.consequence: The controlled observation type END_BIN is the last native base-bin record inside a report interval. It is NOT a mathematical instantaneous point. A true point operator appears only in the synthetic analytical unit tests.

timestamp_anchor_note.issue: The UCI documentation states the values are minute-averaged but does not say whether the printed timestamp labels the start or the end of that minute.
timestamp_anchor_note.adopted_convention: The record labelled t is treated as the mean over [t, t+1min).
timestamp_anchor_note.why_this_does_not_affect_the_comparison: The two possible anchors differ by a uniform 1-minute shift of the entire labelled grid. Every base bin, forecast origin, history window and target window in this pilot is defined on that single labelled grid, so the shift moves all of them together. It cannot change the ordering or adjacency of bins, cannot move an aggregation window across a forecast origin or a split boundary, and is identical for R, M and O. It changes only the wall-clock interpretation of the results, which is recorded as a limitation.
timestamp_anchor_note.not_resolved_by: No inference from the shape of the values was used to pick the anchor.

shared_base_grid.jena: the native 10-minute record is the base bin, unchanged
shared_base_grid.uci: a base bin is the mean of its 10 native minute means, and is missing unless all 10 are present
shared_base_grid.resulting_semantics: for both datasets a base bin holds the INTERVAL_MEAN of the physical quantity over that 10-minute bin
